page: Microsoft Azure L2as_v4 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

For local storage, the L2as_v4 includes a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. Benchmark data reveals a distinct asymmetry between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3077.27 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2034.0, both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is weak, with the stress-ng multi-core metric matching the single-core score at 3077.27, and Geekbench multi-core scoring at 2584.0. Memory bandwidth also exhibits constraints, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 151.28 GB/sec, while large block write bandwidth remains average at 27.68 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and dedicated AMD EPYC hardware, the L2as_v4 offers a resource-dense configuration for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel CPU scaling. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast local scratch space, though database operations scored poorly in Passmark benchmarks. This server is best suited for lightweight memory-optimized tasks, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving where single-core performance is prioritized over multi-threaded throughput.
description: The Microsoft Azure L2as_v4 is a memory-optimized, x86_64 virtual machine from the Lasv4 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads), 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD with Premium Storage capability. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth are weak, reflecting the single-core physical limitation. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-dense, low-concurrency workloads. It is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight memory-intensive tasks, and basic text processing.
